newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul panel favours higher bank ownership - papers.
newsitem.headline: Seoul panel favours higher bank ownership - papers.

text.p: A South Korean panel will propose raising the individual shareholding limit in banks, reversing an earlier decision, local newspapers reported on Saturday.
The Maeil Business Newspaper reported the special panel reviewing financial reform measures had decided to raise the ceiling to 10 percent from the current four percent in all nationwide banks.
But prior government approval will be required for banks seeking an expansion in individual ownership, it said.
The current 15 percent limit on provincial banks will remain unchanged, the newspaper said.
On Tuesday, the Presidential Commission for Financial Reform announced it had decided to uphold the four percent ceiling.
It also said on Tuesday it would propose expanding the ceiling to 10 percent only when banks were newly opened or when other financial institutions shift into banking.
Officials at the commission were not immediately available for comment.
